## R Markdown

```{r}
f <- "data/Redacted-2023Coordinated-CVR.xlsx"

# Read the three header rows (rows 2, 3 and 4); skip = 1 ignores only row 1
hdr <- read_excel(f, skip = 1, n_max = 3, col_names = FALSE, col_types = "text")

# Join: row 4 first, then row 2 (the contest), then row 3 (the choice)
# hdr[1, ] is row 2, hdr[2, ] is row 3, hdr[3, ] is row 4
new_names <- paste(hdr[3, ], hdr[1, ], hdr[2, ], sep = "_")

# Delete the leftover "NA" pieces from empty cells
new_names <- gsub("NA_|_NA", "", new_names)

# Read the real data (row 5 onward) with the new names
cvr <- read_excel(f, skip = 4, col_names = new_names)

# Check the result
names(cvr)
```

```{r}
colnames(cvr)
```

```{r}
cvr <- cvr |>
  clean_names()

colnames(cvr)
```


### 1. - Maya

"According to the analysis by Boulder Reporting Lab, approximately 19% of voters cast their ballots for the entire Boulder Elevated slate, exclusively voting for its candidates."

For this finding, we can filter the data for people who voted exclusively for Bob Yates for mayor and for Terri Brncic, Jennifer (Jenny) Robins, Tina Marquis, and Tara Winer for city council. The 19% statistic corrects some people's perception that most voters cast ballots for one slate of candidates.

The entire cvr dataset we're working with has 118,787 observations (aka rows). This will be the denominator for getting the percentage.

From below work: 6,522 obs (aka rows aka people) voted exclusively for the Boulder Elevated slate.

6,522/118,787 = 0.0549 = 5.5 % -> far from 19%. What went wrong?

Denominator too big? Looked into it more. This data is for the whole county, not just Boulder City.

So I found the denominator we want from this webpage https://bouldervotes.org/2023.html : "34,249 city ballots counted."

--> 6,522/34,249 = 0.1904289176 = 19%

ChatGPT Convo: https://chatgpt.com/share/6acf194b-6cc0-83e9-bbbe-7a957b454a5a

* **Analysis summary**: See above explanation. Calculated the desired 19% by dividing the number of people who voted for council members Terri Brncic, Jenny Robins, Tina Marquis, and Tara Winer; and who ranked Bob Yates number one of the four mayoral candidates-- by the number of Boulder City ballots cast.

```{r}
cvr_candidates_sentence_one <- cvr |>
  filter(
    city_of_boulder_mayoral_candidates_number_of_positions_1_number_of_ranks_4_bob_yates_1 == 1,
    city_of_boulder_council_candidates_vote_for_4_terri_brncic == 1,
    city_of_boulder_council_candidates_vote_for_4_jenny_robins == 1,
    city_of_boulder_council_candidates_vote_for_4_tina_marquis == 1,
    city_of_boulder_council_candidates_vote_for_4_tara_winer == 1
  ) |>
  group_by(cvr_number)
```

### 2. - Seann

"And about 29% of voters cast their ballots for the entire Boulder Progressive’s slate of candidates. Because Boulder Progressives only endorsed two city council candidates, this percentage includes ballots where voters supported any of the other candidates, including those endorsed by Boulder Elevated or those who were not endorsed by either of the two committees: Silas Atkins, Waylon Lewis, Aaron Gabriel Neyer, and Jacques Decalo."

* **Analysis summary**: I came up with this specific code chunk as it allowed me to filter out specifically the progressive candidates of the 2023 races. Filtering out which voters ranked any of these candidates as #1 allowed me to calculate the percentage of voters who cast their votes for the progressive slate. This includes both progressive mayoral candidates and both progressive council candidates. This code chunk displays the voters that ranked Aaron Brockett or Nicole Speer as #1 in the mayoral election, showcasing who placed a Progressive candidate at the top. This code also shows the voters who cast their ballots for Taishya Adams and Ryan Schuchard for Boulder City Council.

```{r}
# Put code to reverse engineer sentence here
cvr |>
filter(
    `city_of_boulder_mayoral_candidates_number_of_positions_1_number_of_ranks_4_aaron_brockett_1` == 1, 
    `city_of_boulder_mayoral_candidates_number_of_positions_1_number_of_ranks_4_nicole_speer_1` == 1, 
    `city_of_boulder_council_candidates_vote_for_4_taishya_adams` == 1,
    `city_of_boulder_council_candidates_vote_for_4_ryan_schuchard` == 1 
  )
# Display results of code below this codeblock
```


### 3. 

“All the candidates who were endorsed by Boulder Progressives opposed the Safe Zones 4 Kids ballot measure. Even so, about 26% of voters who backed the Boulder Progressives’ slate of candidates also supported the Safe Zones 4 Kids ballot measure. By comparison, about 88% of voters who only supported the Boulder Elevated slate of candidates also voted for the Safe Zones 4 Kids measure. All the Boulder Elevated-endorsed candidates backed the measure.”

### 4.

“Two other unofficial candidate committees, meanwhile — Better Boulder and Sierra Club Indian Peaks — endorsed a different mix of candidates: Brockett for mayor and Adams, Schuchard, Winer and Lewis for city council. Less than 5% of voters voted for this exact slate of candidates.”

### 5.

“Separately, more than 2,600 City of Boulder ballots did not include a vote for any city council candidates. The fourth seat on the Boulder City Council was decided by 46 votes.”
